title: Pixel Perfect Manifest
description: Index of the files written by a render: the options it was made with and, for every exported resource, where its images are and how to read them. Written to <output-path>/manifest.json. Fields with a default may be omitted; consumers must treat a missing field as its default and ignore fields they do not know.
$comment: Engine: keys sorted, pretty-printed, ending with a newline; byte-identical for identical renders.

$schema.description: Optional path or URL of this schema, for editors and third-party tools.

files.description: One entry per exported resource. Empty when the worksheet has nothing to export.
files.$comment: Engine: entries sorted by id; ids are unique.

options.description: The command-line options the render was made with. Entries in files can be read without them, but scale is needed to recover source pixel sizes (width / scale).
options.$comment: Open on purpose: new command-line options are added here without a new schema version.

format.description: Output image format, as given by --format (e.g. "png", "webp").
format.$comment: Not an enum on purpose: new formats do not change the contract.

scale.description: Integer upscale factor (--scale): every source pixel became a scale×scale block. width and height in files are already scaled; source size in pixels is width / scale, use it to set pixels-per-unit when importing.

safeBuild.description: Whether --safe-build was used, i.e. files are named by a hash of their id instead of the id itself. Hashed names are stable as long as the id is unchanged.

singleFrames.description: Whether animations were written as one image per frame (kind frameCollection) instead of a single animated image.

path.description: Path of an image file, relative to the output path, with / separators.

fractional.description: Duration in seconds as an exact fraction num/den, so it can be converted to milliseconds, ticks or frames without accumulated rounding.
fractional.$comment: Engine: reduced to lowest terms; always > 0, since every worksheet duration is at least one frame-unit.

index.description: Position of the frame in playback order, from 0.

duration.description: How long the frame is shown; always > 0.

render.description: An exported resource and the file(s) written for it. kind says which other fields are present.

id.description: Export pointer of the resource, /<collection>/<id>, with the id as written in the worksheet (it may contain /). Stable key for referencing the resource from game code; use it instead of path.

width.description: Image width in pixels, after scaling. For a frameCollection, the width of every frame.

height.description: Image height in pixels, after scaling. For a frameCollection, the height of every frame.

kind.description: How the resource was written: static, a single still image (path); animation, a single animated image (path, frameCount, loop); frameCollection, one image per frame (frames, loop).

then.description: The resource is a static image, exported as a single file.
The resource is an animation, exported as a single file.

frameCount.description: Number of frames in the animated image.

loop.description: Length of one loop of the animation.

then.description: The resource is an animation, exported as a group of files each containing a full frame.

frames.description: The frame images; array order is playback order.
frames.$comment: Engine: frames sorted by index, indices 0..n-1 without gaps; durations sum to loop.

loop.description: Length of one loop; the sum of the frame durations.
